intro: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is 168 letters long, the longest place name in the world according to Guinness World Records.
Every ninth lunar month, Phuket's Peranakan Chinese community gives up meat for nine days for the Vegetarian Festival, with street processions that go on for days.
Chiang Mai's old city is an almost perfect square, its moat dug when King Mangrai founded the city in 1296.
At the 2019 New Year auction in Tokyo, a single bluefin tuna sold for ¥333.6 million, about US$3 million.
Osaka was once called "the nation's kitchen", and its motto is kuidaore: eat until you drop, or until you go broke.
Kyoto was on the shortlist of atomic-bomb targets in 1945. US Secretary of War Henry Stimson, who had visited the city and admired its temples, had it taken off.
Hong Kong's Central–Mid-Levels escalator is the longest outdoor covered escalator system in the world: about 800 m, running downhill in the morning and uphill the rest of the day.
Shanghai runs the world's first commercial high-speed maglev: it floats the 30 km to Pudong Airport in about eight minutes.
In 2016 a Singapore hawker stall selling soya sauce chicken rice for about S$2 won a MICHELIN star. Its hawker culture is on UNESCO's heritage list.
